Editorial update · October 2026 · Source-backed


## How to evaluate Jellyfish against Waydev


Jellyfish emphasizes engineering investment allocation and has expanded AI impact analysis. Its October 2026 announcement describes lifecycle exploration, AI skill adoption, and AI spend-to-work attribution. It is inaccurate to describe Jellyfish as having no AI measurement or no engineering reporting.


**Best-fit decision:** Choose Jellyfish when engineering investment allocation and executive portfolio visibility dominate. Evaluate Waydev when private deployment requirements, configurable engineering dashboards, AI code-to-production analysis, and integrated delivery metrics are central. Verify each capability in a current product demonstration.

## Jellyfish alternatives and competitors: quick verdict for 2027 planning


**Comparing Jellyfish competitors?** Evaluate Waydev, Swarmia, DX and other platforms by the engineering decision you need to support—not just a features checklist.[Jellyfish currently describes](https://jellyfish.co/) AI ROI, investment allocation, custom metrics, agents and DevEx surveys; do not assume it lacks these capabilities.


- **Choose a Jellyfish evaluation** if engineering investment allocation, AI ROI reporting, benchmarking and executive-facing metrics are your primary shortlist criteria.
- **Evaluate Waydev** if DORA/SPACE/DX delivery context, AI adoption and impact, Signals, Prompt Dashboards or an[air-gapped 15B Waydev Brain option](https://waydev.co/waydev-brain/) are required.
- **Planning a Jellyfish replacement?** Map Jira and Git identities, historical baselines, AI cost attribution, approvals and stakeholder reports before comparing pricing or migration effort. Follow the[Jellyfish-to-Waydev migration guide](https://waydev.co/migrating-from-jellyfish-to-waydev-when-allocation-reporting-stops-being-enough/) .


**Buyer test:** Have both vendors reproduce the same quarterly AI-spend-to-delivery report with source-level traceability, role-based access and documented data gaps.[Request Waydev’s enterprise evaluation](https://waydev.co/demo/) .


Based on public product descriptions, October 2026. Validate current offerings, security architecture and pricing directly with each vendor.


**Short answer.** Both platforms read the same raw signals from Git and Jira without asking engineers to log anything. Jellyfish is built around engineering investment and financial reporting for the board. Waydev is built around delivery, developer experience and AI impact, with self-hosted deployment and an open API for teams that need the data in their own systems.


If your first question is “what did we spend engineering on last quarter,” Jellyfish answers it well. If it is “where is delivery breaking down, and what is AI actually doing to our throughput and quality,” that is where[Waydev](https://waydev.co/) is built to go deeper.


Waydev is a software engineering intelligence platform for engineering leaders. It connects to your version control and issue tracking systems, then surfaces what you need to improve delivery speed, team health and planning accuracy.[Request an enterprise demo](https://waydev.co/demo/) .

## Where Waydev goes further


**You can run it inside your own perimeter** Waydev offers cloud and on-premise deployment, with self-hosted Git and ticketing integrations on the Enterprise plan. For regulated industries and organizations that will not send commit data to a vendor cloud, this is usually the deciding factor rather than a feature preference.


**The data does not stay locked in the dashboard** Waydev provides scoped API access to engineering metrics and supports designated input endpoints such as deployments and incidents; confirm endpoint coverage and permissions against the[API reference](https://docs.waydev.co/v5.0/docs/api-docs) . Documented connectors cover Git providers, ticketing systems, CI/CD, code quality and AI coding tools; confirm the required integrations in[Waydev’s supported tool stack](https://docs.waydev.co/docs/supported-integrations) .


**Code quality sits next to delivery data** Waydev pulls Sonar data so quality metrics appear alongside issue tracking and version control. Speed without a quality reading beside it is the most common way a metrics program misleads its owner.


**AI impact, not just AI adoption**[Waydev Brain](https://waydev.co/waydev-brain/) and[Signals](https://waydev.co/features/signals/) surface where AI tooling is changing throughput, review load and quality, rather than reporting seat counts. Adoption is easy to measure and tells you very little on its own.


**Scale and customization** Waydev supports customizable dashboards, metrics and team filters for enterprise engineering organizations; confirm contributor scale, deployment options and reporting requirements in a proof of concept.


**Evaluate Waydev before committing** Waydev runs a proof of concept on your own repositories before any purchase, and publishes pricing. Jellyfish requires a sales conversation to see either.


## Where Jellyfish is the better fit


Every honest comparison has this section. Here is ours.


Jellyfish is strong when the primary audience for engineering data is the finance organization and the board. Its investment allocation and software capitalization tooling is mature, it has been recognized as a leader in G2’s software development analytics category for seventeen consecutive quarters, and its executive dashboards are built for exactly that conversation.3


If your top three questions are all about R&D spend classification, capitalization and initiative-level cost reporting, Jellyfish is a reasonable choice. Waydev is the stronger fit when delivery health, developer experience, AI impact and deployment control matter more than accounting output.

## Inside the Waydev platform


Waydev is organized into four modules. Each answers a different question, and they read from the same commit-level source.


### Delivery


Measure, optimize and improve every stage of software delivery.


**[Pull Request Insights](https://waydev.co/pull-request-insights/)** Visualize every PR, find where reviews stall, and isolate the specific roadblocks behind a slow stage.


**[DORA metrics](https://waydev.co/dora-metrics/)** Deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore, tracked as a trend rather than a snapshot.


**Cycle time** How quickly work moves from first commit to delivery, broken into coding, review and deployment so you can see which stage is actually costing you.


Cycle time split by stage, which is where the bottleneck usually becomes obvious.


### Health


Team dynamics, working practices and the conditions behind delivery numbers.


**[Developer Experience](https://waydev.co/features/developer-experience-dx/)** The friction your contributors hit day to day, which is the part delivery metrics never explain on their own.


**Team and contributor insights** A summary of recent activity by team and by person, built for understanding load distribution rather than ranking individuals.


**Benchmark and hygiene** How teams compare against company standards, and whether work is being tracked consistently enough for the rest of the data to be trustworthy.


### Planning


Align engineering work with product and business strategy.


**Resource planning** Where engineering capacity is allocated, what it costs, and how key initiatives are progressing against that allocation.


**Project costs** Cost and progress on key initiatives and deliverables, so schedule conversations happen before the slip rather than after it.


### Automation


Targets track key metrics against benchmarks, and notifications fire when a team hits a milestone or a threshold moves the wrong way. The[work log](https://waydev.co/features/work-log/) removes the guesswork about where effort actually went.


## How Jellyfish approaches the same problem


Jellyfish gathers engineering signals from commits and pull requests in Git and from tasks in Jira, then layers contextual data from calendars, product planning tools and HR systems to build a picture of what teams are working on and how long it takes.


The output is oriented toward allocation: work and resources mapped to projects, releases and business objectives. Their main reports cover alignment, investment distribution across roadmap, unplanned, infrastructure and support work, technical debt, product pillars, and productivity. Like Waydev, it requires no manual input from engineers.

## Common questions


### Does Jellyfish offer DORA metrics?


Yes. Jellyfish tracks DORA metrics including lead time, deployment frequency and mean time to resolution.1 DORA coverage alone is not a reason to choose between the two platforms. Deployment model, data portability and depth of developer experience data are.


### Is SOC 3 a higher level of certification than SOC 2?


No, and it is worth stating plainly. A SOC 3 report can only be issued after a clean SOC 2 Type II audit, and it is a public-facing summary of that same examination.4 The practical benefit is that Waydev’s SOC 3 report can be shared freely without an NDA, while a SOC 2 report typically cannot. Both platforms hold SOC 2.


### Can we migrate historical data?


Waydev backfills from your existing version control and issue tracking history, up to 6 months on Pro and 36 months on Premium, so trend analysis starts on day one rather than after a quarter of collection.


### Do engineers have to change how they work?


No, for either platform. Both read signals that your Git provider and issue tracker already produce.


### Which is better for a finance-led reporting requirement?


Jellyfish, if software capitalization and R&D spend classification are the primary use case. Waydev, if delivery performance, developer experience and AI impact carry more weight than accounting output.


## Compare the two on your own data


The fastest way to settle a platform decision is to point both at the same repositories and see which one answers your actual questions. Waydev runs that as a proof of concept before any commitment.

## How to choose a Jellyfish alternative in 2027


**Updated buyer’s verdict (October 2026):** Jellyfish deserves consideration where R&D portfolio allocation and investment reporting are central. Shortlist Waydev when engineering delivery, AI adoption and impact, and customizable stakeholder views are the main evaluation priorities.


**What Jellyfish already does:** Jellyfish discusses engineering investment allocation and has published an AI investment-versus-output measurement approach that includes spend, adoption, output and business-alignment indicators. Treat this as a substantive competitor capability.[Check the competitor’s own documentation](https://jellyfish.co/library/ai-investment-vs-engineering-output/) .


**What to test in a proof of value:** During a pilot, trace one business initiative from issue or PR through released work and team cost in both systems; verify how investment categories are assigned and whether source records support the result.


### Is Jellyfish limited to engineering investment allocation?


No. Jellyfish also describes AI measurement and engineering output. Compare both platforms on the specific investment and delivery analysis your executives require.


**Evidence standard:** These are editorial assessments, not a validated hands-on benchmark. Feature availability, pricing and implementation requirements may differ by plan or configuration. Request the same live demonstration and measure with identical definitions before selecting either vendor.


**Decision in brief:** Prioritize a platform that can demonstrate impact using your organization’s real engineering data. During the trial, evaluate investment allocation, project outcomes, delivery health and the financial interpretation of AI-assisted engineering. Avoid comparing platforms on a single dashboard screenshot or vendor marketing claims.


### What Jellyfish offers today


Jellyfish publicly emphasizes engineering investment allocation, business alignment, delivery management and team health. Compare the quality of those workflows rather than claiming it lacks strategic reporting.[Vendor source and product details](https://jellyfish.co/platform/engineering-management-platform/) .


### Waydev features to inspect during your comparison


The images below are existing Waydev media assets. Confirm feature availability, account permissions and the precise metrics in your environment during a demo.


Waydev Team Insights — review team-level engineering trends and where work slows down.[Explore the feature](https://waydev.co/features/team-insights/) . Waydev AI ROI feature illustration — investigate AI tool costs alongside measured delivery changes; actual ROI depends on data and attribution assumptions.[Explore the feature](https://waydev.co/features/ai-roi/) .


### Five criteria for a fair enterprise comparison


1. **Delivery evidence:** Require consistent definitions for cycle time, deployment frequency, change failures and rework.
2. **AI impact and ROI:** Separate licensed seats and AI usage from verified production outcomes and fully loaded costs.
3. **Developer experience:** Assess friction, review queues, qualitative feedback and whether metrics discourage gaming.
4. **Enterprise fit:** Validate integrations, role-based access, data retention, security reviews and deployment constraints.
5. **Proof of value:** Agree on a baseline, real teams and success criteria before starting a pilot.


### Questions to ask in a Jellyfish vs Waydev demo


- Can leaders trace investment allocation to work actually delivered?
- How are AI adoption, team outcomes and financial assumptions connected?
- Which forecasts and portfolio views can be validated during a pilot?


### When is Waydev worth evaluating?


Consider Waydev when you need to investigate DORA and developer-experience trends alongside AI adoption, delivery outcomes and business impact. The right choice depends on your workflow, integrations, governance and which outcomes you need to prove; request a side-by-side pilot using your own data rather than relying on blanket feature claims.
